```{python}
#| output: false
import io
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import requests
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_line, geom_abline,
    labs, theme_minimal,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display

LG = "mbb"
PBP_TAG = "espn_mens_college_basketball_pbp"
DL = "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download"
season = 2026
# An era the booster never saw: the bundled in-game booster is fit on a single
# season (2023) of game state; 2012 was played under the 35-second shot clock
# and the pre-2019 three-point line -- a different rule era, not just a
# different season.
HOLDOUT = 2012


def fetch_pbp(s):
    r = requests.get(f"{DL}/{PBP_TAG}/play_by_play_{s}.parquet", timeout=600)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return pl.read_parquet(io.BytesIO(r.content))


def evaluate(pbp):
    """Join every play to its game's realized outcome and return the calibration pieces."""
    final = (
        pbp.sort("sequence_number")
        .group_by("game_id")
        .agg(pl.col("home_score").last().alias("final_home"),
             pl.col("away_score").last().alias("final_away"))
        .with_columns((pl.col("final_home") > pl.col("final_away")).cast(pl.Float64).alias("home_won"))
        .filter(pl.col("final_home") != pl.col("final_away"))
    )
    df = pbp.join(final.select("game_id", "home_won"), on="game_id", how="inner")
    p = df["home_win_prob"].to_numpy()
    y = df["home_won"].to_numpy()
    bins = np.clip((p * 20).astype(int), 0, 19)
    rows = []
    for b in range(20):
        m = bins == b
        if m.sum() > 0:
            rows.append({"bin_mid": (b + 0.5) / 20, "pred": float(p[m].mean()),
                         "obs": float(y[m].mean()), "n": int(m.sum())})
    cal = pl.DataFrame(rows)
    pre = df.group_by("game_id").agg(pl.col("pregame_home_prob").first(), pl.col("home_won").first())
    return {
        "df": df, "final": final, "cal": cal,
        "brier": float(np.mean((p - y) ** 2)),
        "cal_mae": float((cal["pred"] - cal["obs"]).abs().mean()),
        "base_brier": float(np.mean((final["home_won"].mean() - y) ** 2)),
        "pre_brier": float(pre.select(((pl.col("pregame_home_prob") - pl.col("home_won")) ** 2).mean()).item()),
    }


pbp = fetch_pbp(season)
ev = evaluate(pbp)
df, final, cal, brier, cal_mae = ev["df"], ev["final"], ev["cal"], ev["brier"], ev["cal_mae"]

hold_raw = fetch_pbp(HOLDOUT)
if "home_win_prob" in hold_raw.columns:
    hold_src = "the published release columns"
    hold_pbp = hold_raw
else:
    # The release asset currently lacks the WP columns (the 2026-08 strip
    # incident, see Provenance). Apply the same bundled booster here so the
    # unseen era is still evaluated on the shipped plays.
    from sportsdataverse.mbb import build_mbb_season_wp
    hold_src = "probabilities computed at render time -- the release asset lacks the WP columns"
    hold_pbp = build_mbb_season_wp(HOLDOUT)
del hold_raw
hv = evaluate(hold_pbp)


def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))
```

The MBB rule-era win-probability suite (trained, bundled, and oracle-gated
in sdv-py) is applied **in place** to every published season of
`espn_mens_college_basketball_pbp`: `home_win_prob` and the pregame prior
(`pregame_home_prob`) are added to each play with every original column
preserved. The published pbp itself is how the model reaches consumers —
there is no separate WP asset to fall out of sync with the plays.

The model is an XGBoost classifier over game state — score margin, seconds
left (and its square root), the pregame logit, and possession — fit on a
single season (2023). Operationally the enrichment **is** the pbp publisher:
`scripts/daily_mbb_data_processor.sh` builds the plain season pbp into the
tree and never uploads it; stage `mbb_model_03_wp_enrich` reads the tree
pbp/schedules/team_box, appends the two columns and publishes
parquet+csv+rds; and `mbb_data_build.publish` refuses any pbp parquet
without finite WP columns, asserted on the file about to upload. That design
closes a recorded incident: the old publish-plain-then-re-enrich order
stripped the columns off the release on every nightly, and the 2026-08-26
whole-history republish stripped 2003–2023 outright (2024–2026 were
re-enriched by the in-season nightly). Until those seasons are republished,
this document computes the holdout era's probabilities itself and says so.

This document is the model's **out-of-band evaluation**: it downloads a full
published season at render time and holds the in-game probabilities against
each game's realized outcome — first in-era, then for an era the booster
never saw. If the enrichment ever regressed, went stale, or was stripped, the
calibration sections below would show it on the next render.

## Evaluation data

```{python}
tbl = pl.DataFrame({
    "season": [season],
    "enriched_plays": [df.height],
    "games": [int(df["game_id"].n_unique())],
    "home_win_rate": [float(final["home_won"].mean())],
    "mean_home_win_prob": [float(df["home_win_prob"].mean())],
})
gt_show(
    GT(tbl.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Published season evaluated at render time — {season}",
                subtitle="every play of the published pbp joined to its game's realized outcome (ties from data artifacts excluded)")
    .fmt_number(columns=["enriched_plays"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_percent(columns=["home_win_rate"], decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns=["mean_home_win_prob"], decimals=4)
)
```

The mean predicted probability sitting close to the realized home-win rate
is the zeroth-order calibration check; the college home floor is one of the
strongest in sports and both numbers reflect it.

## Calibration

```{python}
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame({
        "metric": ["Brier score (all plays)", "20-bin calibration MAE",
                   "baseline Brier (constant home-win rate)"],
        "value": [brier, cal_mae, ev["base_brier"]],
    }).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Out-of-band calibration — {season} published season")
    .fmt_number(columns="value", decimals=4)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Reliability diagram, 20 bins — predicted in-game probability vs realized outcome frequency."
(
    ggplot(cal.to_pandas(), aes("pred", "obs"))
    + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="gray")
    + geom_point(aes(size="n"), color="#2a6f97") + geom_line(color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="predicted home win probability", y="observed home win frequency",
           title=f"WP reliability — {season} ({df.height:,} plays)")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
per = (
    df.group_by("period_number")
    .agg(pl.len().alias("plays"),
         ((pl.col("home_win_prob") - pl.col("home_won")) ** 2).mean().alias("brier"))
    .sort("period_number")
    .filter(pl.col("plays") > 10000)
)
gt_show(
    GT(per.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Brier by period — uncertainty should resolve as the game progresses",
                subtitle="a well-behaved WP model gets sharper (lower Brier) in later periods")
    .fmt_number(columns="plays", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns="brier", decimals=4)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "The season's wildest game by WP swing: in-game home win probability trace."
sw = (
    df.group_by("game_id")
    .agg((pl.col("home_win_prob").diff().abs().sum()).alias("swing"),
         pl.col("home_team_name").first(), pl.col("away_team_name").first())
    .sort("swing", descending=True).head(1)
)
gid = sw["game_id"][0]
g = df.filter(pl.col("game_id") == gid).sort("sequence_number").with_row_index("play_no")
title = f"{sw['away_team_name'][0]} at {sw['home_team_name'][0]} — most volatile game of {season}"
(
    ggplot(g.to_pandas(), aes("play_no", "home_win_prob"))
    + geom_line(color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="play number", y="home win probability", title=title)
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame({
        "model": ["pregame prior (one prob per game)", "in-game WP (all plays)"],
        "brier": [ev["pre_brier"], brier],
    }).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Pregame vs in-game — the value the enrichment adds over the prior")
    .fmt_number(columns="brier", decimals=4)
)
```

The reliability diagram hugging the diagonal, the per-period Brier falling
monotonically, and the in-game model beating its own pregame prior are the
three signatures of a healthy applied WP surface. The volatile-game trace is
the demonstration consumers care about: the column tells the story of a
comeback without any narrative input.

## Unseen-era holdout

```{python}
display(Markdown(
    f"Holdout season **{HOLDOUT}** — {hv['df'].height:,} plays in "
    f"{hv['df']['game_id'].n_unique():,} games; probabilities from {hold_src}."
))
eras = pl.DataFrame({
    "era": [f"{season} (in-era)", f"{HOLDOUT} (unseen: 35-second shot clock, old three-point line)"],
    "plays": [df.height, hv["df"].height],
    "brier": [brier, hv["brier"]],
    "baseline_brier": [ev["base_brier"], hv["base_brier"]],
    "skill_vs_baseline": [1 - brier / ev["base_brier"], 1 - hv["brier"] / hv["base_brier"]],
    "calibration_mae_20bin": [cal_mae, hv["cal_mae"]],
    "pregame_brier": [ev["pre_brier"], hv["pre_brier"]],
})
gt_show(
    GT(eras.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Era transfer — the same booster in-era and on an era it never saw",
                subtitle="the calibration-MAE gap between the rows is the era-transfer error, bounded here rather than assumed")
    .fmt_number(columns="plays", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns=["brier", "baseline_brier", "calibration_mae_20bin", "pregame_brier"], decimals=4)
    .fmt_percent(columns="skill_vs_baseline", decimals=1)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Reliability, in-era vs unseen era. A curve that stays on the diagonal in the old era means the game-state features transfer across rule changes; a bowed curve is the era-transfer error made visible."
both = pl.concat([
    cal.with_columns(pl.lit(f"{season} in-era").alias("era")),
    hv["cal"].with_columns(pl.lit(f"{HOLDOUT} unseen era").alias("era")),
])
(
    ggplot(both.to_pandas(), aes("pred", "obs", color="era"))
    + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="gray")
    + geom_point(aes(size="n")) + geom_line()
    + labs(x="predicted home win probability", y="observed home win frequency",
           title="WP reliability by era")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

The booster sees only game state, so what an unseen era tests is whether
"down 6 with 4:00 left" meant the same thing under a 35-second clock. The
table bounds that explicitly: the skill-versus-baseline and calibration MAE
of the old era sit next to the in-era numbers rather than being assumed
equal. The pregame prior also moves across eras — it is an as-of team-rating
model over that season's own results — so the holdout tests the whole
applied surface, not just the tree.

## Provenance & reproducibility

- **Model:** XGBoost in-game WP over game state (score margin, seconds left,
  its square root, pregame logit, possession), fit on the 2023 season,
  bundled and oracle-gated in sdv-py (`mbb/models/mbb_in_game_wp.ubj`).
- **Applied to:** every published season of
  `espn_mens_college_basketball_pbp`, in place, columns
  `home_win_prob` + `pregame_home_prob`, by the enrichment stage — the pbp
  asset's only publisher. `mbb_data_build.publish.assert_wp_enriched`
  refuses any pbp parquet missing the columns or below a 0.999 finite-rate
  floor (observed 1.0 on 2024–2026), asserted on the file about to upload.
- **Pipeline:** `scripts/mbb_models.sh 03` → stage
  `python/mbb_model_03_wp_enrich.py -s <season> -e <season> --base ../mbb`,
  wired at the end of `scripts/daily_mbb_data_processor.sh` (after
  schedules + team_box exist in the tree). Single home: `models/manifest.yaml`.
- **Release state (2026-09-01):** 2024–2026 carry the columns; 2003–2023 lost
  them to the 2026-08-26 whole-history republish and need one
  `mbb_model_03_wp_enrich -s 2003 -e 2023` republish. This document falls
  back to computing the holdout era itself while that is outstanding.
- **This document** evaluates two published seasons downloaded at render
  time (~90 MB + ~50 MB) — the exact frames consumers read.
- **Rebuild:** `scripts/render_model_docs.sh` (Quarto → GFM;
  `uv sync --group docs`).

## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **Possession-state features** — foul counts, bonus state, and timeout
  inventory are absent from the WP inputs.
- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #25):** the nightly publish no longer strips
  the WP columns — the enrichment stage is the pbp asset's only publisher
  and the publish path refuses an un-enriched pbp parquet, so no publish
  window exists in which a season lacks WP. The 2003–2023 seasons stripped
  by the 2026-08-26 history republish still need the one-off republish
  listed above.
- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #25):** season-holdout curve — the
  unseen-era section above renders the same calibration for a season the
  booster never saw and reports the era-transfer error as a number.
